name: Proofreading & copyediting (category)
summary: Checking and correcting other people's writing for errors, clarity and style, as an employee or freelancer; a recognized Canadian occupation with a national association and certification.
whatYouDo: Proofreaders catch spelling, grammar and formatting errors in near-final text; copyeditors also fix consistency, clarity and style. Freelancers find clients through directories, platforms (e.g. Scribbr), publishers and referrals, and charge by the hour, word or project.
appeal: High self-employment share: Job Bank reports 39% of Ontario editors are self-employed (vs 15% across occupations)
Clear professional route in Canada via Editors Canada (directory listing and certification)
Job Bank national wage range for editors $20–$50/hour (median about $34.62)
watchOuts: Job Bank says the occupation usually requires a university degree
Job Bank outlook 2025–2027 is 'Limited' in Ontario and Quebec
Editors Canada directory listing requires paid membership (about $310/yr plus $80/yr profile, plus tax)
Certification exams cost about $450 (members) to $550 (non-members) each, plus annual maintenance fees
Finding freelance clients takes time; no guaranteed work

training.notes: Optional paid professional development and certification through Editors Canada.

compensation.notes: Job Bank wages for Editors (NOC 51110), Canada, 2023–2024 Labour Force Survey reference period: low $20, median ~$34.62, high $50/hour. Mostly employee wages; freelance proofreading rates vary widely.

reliability.notes: Job Bank outlook Limited in ON and QC, Moderate in Ottawa/Outaouais (2025–2027). Freelance volume depends on client base.

fees: Optional: Editors Canada membership ~$310/yr plus $80/yr directory profile (plus tax); certification exams ~$450–$550 each; credential maintenance $25 (members) or $100 (non-members) per year.
applicationSteps: Build skills and samples (style guides, before/after edits)
Consider joining Editors Canada and listing in its Online Directory of Editors
Find clients directly, via publishers, or via editing platforms such as Scribbr
fitsIf: You have strong English (or French) writing skills, love precision, and are willing to build a client base over months.
notFitIf: You need income quickly or dislike close, repetitive reading for errors.

sources.title: Editor in Canada
sources.notes: National median about $34.62/h, range $20–$50 (2023–2024 LFS); occupation usually requires a university degree. Seen via search; page not opened.

sources.title: Editor in Ontario
sources.notes: 2025–2027 outlook Limited (employment decline); search summary reports 39% of Ontario editors are self-employed vs 15% average.

sources.title: Editor in Québec
sources.notes: 2025–2027 outlook Limited; employment expected to remain relatively stable.

sources.title: Fees - Editors Canada
sources.notes: One-year membership $310; optional one-year directory profile $80 (two-year $589/$160); plus sales tax; non-refundable. Directory listing limited to members and student affiliates.

sources.title: Editors Canada Professional Certification
sources.notes: Current exam fee per search summary: $450 per exam for members, $550 for non-members.

sources.title: Editors Canada Professional Certification credential maintenance
sources.notes: Annual credential maintenance fee $25 (members) or $100 (non-members); non-payment removes name from the certified roster.
